frames.narration: Every 15 seconds the collector on the checkout host reads its numbers: requests, errors and latency, each tagged with labels such as host and region. Together they are one sample per series.
The agent batches the samples from the host and puts the batch on the ingest queue. The application never waits for storage.
A writer takes the batch and appends each sample to its series in the time-series database. Only the difference from the last timestamp and value is stored, so a sample costs a byte or two.

The error rate climbs after a bad deploy. The rule evaluator runs its query every 30 seconds: 'error ratio for the checkout service over the last 5 minutes'. The result is above the 2% limit for the first time.
The rule says the condition must hold for 5 minutes. A short blip would pass without anyone being woken, so it waits. Evaluation after evaluation, the ratio stays above the limit.
The condition has held for five minutes, so the alert fires. The rule evaluator sends it to the alert manager.
The alert manager sees that 40 hosts have raised the same alert and groups them into one notification. It checks that nothing is silenced, and routes it to the on-call engineer of the checkout team.

The engineer opens a dashboard. Those graphs are served by the query service from a cache plus the latest few seconds from the database, so they load at once. The deploy is rolled back and the error rate falls, and the alert resolves itself.
